{{nihongo|'''Ogawaizumisui Shrine'''|小河泉水神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

'''Ogawa Izumi Suijin Shrine''' (おがわいずみすいじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Yukawa, {{ill|Shimizu, Shizuoka|Q1203168|qid=Q1203168|lt=Shimizu Town}}, {{ill|Suntō District, Shizuoka|Q1142259|qid=Q1142259}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It is sometimes written as “O'''gawa''' Izumi Suijin Shrine.”<ref>[http://www.shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4403125 Ogawa Izumi Suijin Shrine] – Shizuoka Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines</ref>

=== Overview ===
The shrine is located in the central area of Shimizu Town, on the eastern bank just before the {{ill|Kakita River|Q6349486|qid=Q6349486}} joins the {{ill|Kano River|Q6364188|qid=Q6364188}}, opposite the ruins of {{ill|Tokura Castle|Q11496230|qid=Q11496230|lt=Tokura Castle}} and Honjōyama Park.

The date of founding is unknown, but it is identified with the namesake {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} known as '''Ogawa Izumi Shrine''' (おがわいずみじんじゃ), and it is listed in the '{{ill|Izu Province Shinkaichō|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}}' as “Junior Fourth Rank Upper, Ogawa Izumi Myōjin,” making it an ancient shrine.<ref name="gen">[https://genbu.net/data/izu/izumi_title.htm Ogawa Izumi Suijin Shrine] – Genbushi</ref><ref name="engi">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140211-01.html Ogawa Izumi Suijin Shrine] – Research on Engishiki Shrines</ref>

During the Edo period, it was enshrined as a {{ill|Kumano shrine|Q3200355|qid=Q3200355}}, and even after being renamed to its current name in the Meiji period, it has retained this character, such as by enshrining Kumano Fusumi no Mikoto, the deity of {{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|Q710359|qid=Q710359}}.<ref name="gen"/><ref name="engi"/>

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 8 ({{ill|1875|Q7764|qid=Q7764}}), it was designated as a village shrine.<ref name="engi"/>
